name: A press office for your company
pitch: Paste your company's website. An agent reads its pages, organises what they say into a fact sheet, a voice guide and the people and products, and writes a first post, which a supervisor checks against the pages.

folders.about: The company's public pages, one document each, saved by fetch_page. The only evidence a draft can rest on.
The agent's working notes: the fact sheet, with the page behind each fact, the voice guide, and the people and products.
Drafts for publication. A supervisor checks each one against the pages in sources/ before it lands.

opening: I'm the press office for the company you named. First I'll read about six of its public pages. Then I'll organise what they say into a fact sheet, a voice guide and a note of its people and products. Then I'll write a first short post introducing the company. A supervisor checks every draft and refuses any claim I can't point to on a page I read.
prompts: A journalist emails: "We hear you're about to be acquired. Can you comment?" Draft a reply.
Draft a short launch post about the company's main product, for its blog.
What would a journalist want to know that the site does not say? List the gaps.
